title: HCP — Remove Directive — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Remove directive operation (HCP 6.4, 5.4; `DELETE /v2/directives/{directiveId}` in HCP 9.2, 9.4.15): a Management Client, acting for the Context Subject or a delegate, removes a directive. HCP defines no schema for this operation; the members come from HCP 9.2 and 9.4.15. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty.

directiveId.description: HCP `directiveId` (the `{directiveId}` path parameter of HCP 9.2): the directive to remove.

accessToken.description: The Management Client's HCP access token (HCP 9.3), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque.

Response.title: HCP — Remove Directive — response payload
Response.description: The directive is removed. Carries HCP's `204 No Content`, which has no body, so the payload is the empty object. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.
